The After-Medicaid-Approval Checklist

What to save, write down and ask now that Mom has been approved.

Download PDF

Mom's Medicaid was approved. The letter is on the kitchen counter, and nobody has said what the family does next. These are the things to save, write down and ask about from here. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something still to pull together or ask, not a sign that anything is wrong.

Save

Write down

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you save, write down and ask. It doesn't say what any letter means, which changes have to be reported, or whether anything affects Mom's Medicaid. Renewal, reporting and recordkeeping requirements vary by state and by case, so those answers come from the Medicaid agency's own notices and from a professional who knows your state's rules. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.

Ready for the next step?

You've saved the letters, written down the dates and lined up what to ask. The planning interview asks about your family's situation and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for Mom's care.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow the federal renewal flyer for people with Medicaid, which says to watch the mail and keep contact information current; the rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
